title: エネルギー固体化学
subtitle: Solid State Chemistry for Energy Conversion and Storage
educationalGoal:
Three general objectives will be addressed in this course:
-Learn about methods to form and analyze solids for energy conversion and storage.
-Acquire the ability to solve problems using the appropriate analysis method.
-Acquire the ability to synthesize and analyze inorganic compounds to fabricate optical, electrical, and magnetic devices.
advice: There will be two quizzes and a final examination during the course. The exercise sheets will be also distributed in the class. All of the exams will be closed-notes and closed-book, although the key equations will be provided on the exam sheets.
books:
Anthony R. West, Solid State Chemistry and Its Applications, Wiley
Peter Atkins, Elements of Physical Chemistry 7th Edition, Oxford University Press
requiredKnowledge:
Student should be familiar with:
1.	Fundamentals of physics and mathematics.
2.	Fundamentals of 1st and 2nd year university chemistry.

activityGoals.body: Understand diffraction methods to determine crystal structures and analytical methods to determine the elements.
Understand the optical, electrical, and magnetic properties of solids.
Understanding the band structure of solids.
Understanding the principles and function of typical optical, electrical, and magnetic devices.
Understanding the role of inorganic solids in energy conversion and storage.

achievementLevels.ideal:
-Describe the crystal structures of solids and apply that knowledge to solve problems.
-Describe the use of diffractometry to analyze the crystal structure of solids and apply the knowledge to solve problems.
-Describe analytical methods used for determining the elemental composition of solids and apply the knowledge to solve problems.
-Describe the electronic band structure of solids and apply the knowledge to solve problems.
-Describe the principles and functions of optical and electronic devices.
achievementLevels.standard:
-Describe the crystal structures of solids.
-Describe the use of diffractometry to analyze the crystal structure of solids.
-Describe analytical methods used to determine the elemental composition of a solid.
-Describe the electronic band structure of solids.
-Describe the principles and functions of optical and electronic devices.
-Describe applications of solids.
